links.reason: The opening item matches: தமியர் உண்டலும் இலரே (182) and பகுத்துண்டு ... எல்லாந் தலை (322). But 182's list at once goes on to dispositions (முனிவிலர், பிறர் அஞ்சுவது அஞ்சி), so 'the shared meal, not an inner disposition, was the first test' overreaches. Kural 322's பல்லுயிர் ஓம்புதல் sits in the chapter on not killing.

183's சிறப்பின் பாலால் தாயும் மனம் திரியும் among பிறப்பு ஓர் அன்ன உடன்வயிற்று children takes Kural 69's mother rejoicing at சான்றோன் one step further, into partiality among siblings. The teaches names that harder consequence correctly. The Kural's சான்றோன் is worth, not strictly learning.

The scene is distinctive and shared: girls at the vengai and a 'tiger' cry that brings men (புலிபுலி என்னும் பூசல் in 48; குறமகள் ... பூசல் ... ஆகொள் வயப்புலி ஆகும் in 52). That 48 turns the alarm into a first meeting while 52's heroine forbids disclosure is true of the two poems. Reading them as one story is the teaches' framing, not a claim in the texts.

234 is a dusk drive home in the rains; it says nothing of a king or of work finished, so 'wish to finish the work' fails for 234. The Kural's வினைகலந்து வென்றீக வேந்தன் fits poem 44, not this one, and the teaches is only the shared homecoming situation.

The image is strongly shared (ஓரில் நெய்தல் கறங்க ஓர்இல் ... முழவின் பாணி; மணப்பறை ... பிணப்பறை). The tension rests on reading இனிய காண்க as worldly good. It can as well mean seeking virtue, which is what Naladiyar 23's உய்ந்துபோம் ஆறு is glossed as, so the incompatibility is not secure.

192's வாழ்தல் இனிதென மகிழ்ந்தன்றும் இலமே ... இன்னாதென்றலும் இலமே is the stance Kural 379 asks for (நன்றாங்கால் நல்லவாக் காண்பவர் அன்றாங்கால் அல்லற்படுவது எவன்). The raft on the flood gives the order (முறைவழி) a picture, as the teaches says. The verse itself does not say ஊழ்; its chapter does.

The legend is shared and distinctive: ஆட்டன் அத்தி, ஆதி மந்தி, காவிரி in both. 222's friend holds up மருதி அன்ன மாண்புகழ் as a fame to seek, 236's wife likens her own distraught search to Manthi's (ஆதி மந்தி போல ... பேதுபெரிது உறல்). These are opposite uses; 'shame' is a light stretch of பேது.
links.text_issue: A236 line 5 இடைனில and line 10 உய்ர்த்தனென் look like misprints (இடைநில, உயிர்த்தனென்).

links.reason: Teaches is right that the grounds differ: 189 argues from the body (உண்பது நாழி உடுப்பவை இரண்டே), Nal. 9 from each failed use (உண்ணான் ... வழங்கான்). But 'kept wealth already lost' rests on one sense of 189's துய்ப்பேம் எனினே தப்புந பலவே, which can mean many duties fail, not that the wealth is lost.

196 does part without rancour (நோயிலர் ஆக நின் புதல்வர்; வெயிலென முனியேன்). But its rebuke blames the giver's false refusal, while Kural 1060 counsels patience because the giver may really lack. That is a qualification, not agreement.

43's man calls leaving மடமை and stays; 53's woman says his heart, which cannot refuse the needy, drove him away (நம்மினும் பொருளே காதலர் காதல்). These are different men in different situations, not incompatible claims. 43 has no woman's voice, so 'refuses to call either grace' overreaches.

Naladiyar 206 sets poor food among kin above rich food from strangers. 197 marvels at small chiefs who eat குற்றடகு and வரகின் சொன்றி yet know a poet's worth (பாடறிந்து ஒழுகும்). 197 never says that meal is given to the poet, so 'a poor meal valued for the regard it is given with' is read into 197.

Both turn on grey hair: 191 answers யாண்டுபல ஆக நரையில ஆகுதல் யாங்கு by naming wife, children, servants, king and சான்றோர், while Nal. 11 says the wise, foreseeing நரை, குழவியிடத்தே துறந்தார். On the stated reading, how to meet age, the answers are opposed, and the note says which reading it depends on.

Both refer to the vadakkiruttal after the back wound at Venni (புறப்புண் நாணி ... வாள் வடக்கு இருந்தனன் in 65; பொருதுபுண் நாணிய சேரலாதன் ... வான்வடக்கிருந்தென in 55). 65 does not mention the சான்றோர் who went with him (அவனொடு செலீஇயர்), and 55 uses exactly them, so the teaches is accurate.

The same word stands in opposed verdicts: இன்னாது அம்ம இவ்வுலகம் with the maker blamed (படைத்தோன் ... பண்பிலாளன்) in 194, against இன்னாதென்றலும் இலமே in 192. On the reading of both as judgments of the world they are incompatible, and the teaches (protest and equanimity side by side) is specific.

The figure is distinctive and shared: a king's town as the likeness of a woman's bangle (அள்ளூர் அன்ன என் ஒண்தொடி; போஒர் அன்ன என் செறிவளை), from the wife's side and from the courtesan's. They differ in use: 46 lets it slip (நெகிழினும் நெகிழ்க), 186 says he cannot break it (உடைத்தலோ இலனே). That supports the teaches' point that the formula does not mark a side.

233 names the feast (உதியஞ் சேரல் பெருஞ்சோறு கொடுத்த ஞான்றை), and Purananuru 2 praises the patron for it (பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய்). The akam poet turns its கூளிச் சுற்றம் into hills crowding on the track. The note says what the akam poet does with it; that the eaters are ghouls fits 2's battle-feast and goes unremarked.
links.text_issue: Purananuru 2 line 23 றுஞ்சும் is a misprint for துஞ்சும்.

links.reason: Kural 335 urges good deeds before the death rattle. 195 addresses the old who have done none, under the coming கணிச்சி, and sets a floor: நல்லது செய்தல் ஆற்றீர் ஆயினும் அல்லது செய்தல் ஓம்புமின் ... நல்லாற்றுப் படூஉம் நெறியுமார் அதுவே. Qualifies fits and the teaches is accurate.

The parallel is real: நுதல் பசந்தன்றே ... நோய்இலராக நம் காதலர் against பசக்கமன் ... நன்னிலையர் ஆவர் எனின். But the colophon also allows 227 to be the heroine's own speech (தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉமாம்), which undoes the claim that the friend's voice was 'absorbed' into the woman's. The history the teaches asserts is not shown.

Both size gossip by a public spectacle: கவ்வை ... கட்டி பொராஅது ஓடிய ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே against அலர் ... திங்களைப் பாம்புகொண்டற்று. It is a shared figure, not an agreement of claims. The teaches' contrast of rout and eclipse is apt, though the line of development is assumed.

784's நகுதல் is laughter (நகுதற் பொருட்டன்று நட்டல்); 860's நகல் is friendliness set against இகல். The link turns on one root in two senses and on the commentator's gloss, so it is a shared word dressed up as a qualification.

475 speaks only of a cart overloaded with feathers (பீலிபெய் சாகாடும் அச்சிறும்). The many weak enemies combining is commentary, as the note itself says. 873 (தமியனாய்ப் பல்லார் பகைகொள்பவன்) connects only through that gloss.

Both refuse the promised quick return: 'இன்னே வருதும்' எனத்தெளித்தோரே ... இன்இள வேனிலும் வாரார் (229) and நின் வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை (1151). The difference the teaches names is real: a retort before parting against proof gathered afterwards from the season.

The shared bit is the exclamation அம்ம with இவ்வுலகம் (உண்டால் அம்ம இவ்வுலகம்; இன்னாது அம்ம இவ்வுலகம்). 182 says the world endures because of the selfless; 194 says it is harsh. These are not opposite claims, so 'the anthology arguing with itself' is a common particle dressed up.

The wording matches closely: தமக்கென முயலா ... பிறர்க்கென முயலுநர் (182) and தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் பண்ணன் (54). A general ideal in kanchi becomes a one-line epithet for a named patron in akam, which is what the teaches says; 'already' is unneeded.

187 dismisses kinds of ground (நாடா ... காடா ... அவலா ... மிசையா) for the goodness of ஆடவர. Kural 737 lists a land's limbs, which is not quite an answer to what makes a land good, so the tension depends on stretching 737. Calling the Kural's land chapter 'material' and later is not shown.

A real puram name: Pannan, patron of 173 (யான்வாழும் நாளும் பண்ணன் வாழிய; பசிப்பிணி மருத்துவன் இல்லம்), appears in 54 as தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் பண்ணன் சிறுகுடி, whose gooseberry gives the simile. The note says what the akam poet does with him; 'Sirukudi' is in 173's colophon, not its text.

399 says the learned love learning on seeing தாம் இன்புறுவது உலகு இன்புற. 650 says those who cannot கற்றது உணர விரித்துரை are scentless flowers. The pairing makes the unstated condition explicit, that the world's delight needs the telling, which is a real qualification.

The rain figure is shared: a whole people's joy at dawn rain after drought (பல்லோர் உவந்த உவகை எல்லாம் என்னுள் பெய்தந்தற்று) and வாழ்வார்க்கு வானம் பயந்தற்று. But in 42 the joy is the friend's, at the hero's coming to marry, and 'the couplet is the compressed form' is the stock restatement.

The link turns on புணர்வு in two senses: union with the beloved in 1155 (நீங்கின் அரிதால் புணர்வு), attaining wealth in 51 (பிரியின் புணர்வது ஆயின்). Both do favour not leaving, which is a real agreement, but the teaches rests on the word play. Its 'what union costs wealth' inverts 51, which weighs what wealth would cost union.

Same poet, same phrase (நீ வெய்யோளொடு), same Kaveri bathing, so the connection is real. But the note misplaces 6: there the bathing is at Thithan's உறந்தை, and மத்தி கழாஅர் is only the likeness for her lost youth (கழாஅர் அன்ன எம் இளமை). The two places swap roles between the poems.

The wording matches: கீழ்ப்பால் ஒருவன் கற்பின் மேற்பால் ஒருவனும் அவன்கண் படுமே (183) against மேற்பிறந்தார் ஆயினும் கல்லாதார் கீழ்ப்பிறந்தும் கற்றார் அனைத்திலர் பாடு (409). The teaches' point that both keep மேல்/கீழ் as the scale that learning overturns, rather than abolishing it, is accurate and specific.

iraicchi.act: the heron, thinking of its lone chick on the njazhal branch, flies home over the backwater
iraicchi.sense: The hero too should think of the lonely girl and come to her.

poems.note: The tusker leaving the vengai's flowering branch desolate (புலம்ப) suggests the hero and the forsaken girl, but the second pair (rage and the drive for wealth) is too thin to count.

iraicchi.act: the crab shuts itself into its mud hole in the cold rains
iraicchi.sense: Even the crab keeps to its home in this season, while he stays away from his.

poems.note: The crab sits in a catalogue of season signs, so a stricter reading would call it mood.

iraicchi.act: the tiger rises at midnight to fetch food for its mate weak after bearing young
iraicchi.sense: The hero, who also comes at midnight, should likewise provide for her by marrying, not part from her.

poems.note: It could also be read as ullurai (night visit and the weak mate as two pairs). It is tagged iraicchi because the carrier is one creature with its mate.
The wind lingering at the door mirrors the hero's long wait outside, but the poem states that wait directly (நெடும்புற நிலை), so no separate sense rises from it.

The pairs: the buffalo churning the clear pond and tearing the ambal is his dalliance, its feeding on kuvalai is his new bride, and its return to the stall with pollen on its back is his coming home marked.

iraicchi.act: the anril does not sleep when its one mate is parted from it
iraicchi.sense: She cannot sleep apart from him, so he must come back.

poems.note: The bird is pointed to inside her quoted words (காண்), but the application to herself is left unstated.

iraicchi.act: the little female bird crosses the heat to a fig that once fed it, finds no fruit and faints remembering the days of plenty
iraicchi.sense: His wife, left without him, pines remembering their days together.

iraicchi.act: the red dog rests with its starving mate in the shade of the hero-stone
iraicchi.sense: Even the wild dog stays by its hungry mate in the waste, yet he left her for wealth.
